scope: Preserve immutable accepted attempt references through evaluation dispatch, notifications, normal-loop post-scripts, --once and auto-GPU consumers.
Validate actual catalog routing, exact current closed source reference and confirmed filesystem effect. Historical source lifecycle is not required to equal today's global lifecycle.
Admit native post_script actions with a source-linked durable LAUNCHING intent and deterministic command/source action identity; no Popen or waits under the short transaction/effect guard.
Keep pending/backlog as independently selected actions bound to current accepted native training when such history exists; explicit pre-native compatibility remains.

cases_summary: Delayed native training A event cannot deliver running retry B as finished.
Delayed A event cannot launch evaluation from B's not-yet-accepted completed training artifact.
launch_eval=None after an already accepted native evaluation cannot mint another plain finished event.
Delayed failed evaluation A event cannot increment the completion counter using newly qualified B.
Real _run_leased post-eval consumer cannot start a post-script after an actual retry invalidates the just-accepted source event.
Immutable value, no mutable __dict__ token.
Wrong/omitted catalog refusals.
Missing effect confirmation refuses delivery.
Native pending/backlog positive controls and historical dependency.
Two scripts use generations 1 then 2, repeat does not restart script 1.
Actual pre-Popen intent blocks real evaluation retry.
Unknown Popen leaves LAUNCHING and cannot replay.
False reaper leaves RUNNING, requested-only stop, no terminal, one reaper call.
Actual --once evaluator wait retains stale event fencing after real retry.
Auto-GPU branch cannot use B's metrics for a delayed real A event.
Real failed native A to retry B at actual downstream eligibility and Path.exists boundaries; the old event cannot append a skip record into B diagnostics.
Actual public notification cache callbacks hold the common source effect guard; external transport and config recovery are outside it.
A real retry request from the actual cache callback is refused by guard contention.
Existing owner or revoked effect confirmation prevents both local native cache writes.
A failing dedup callback is logged as unavailable, not acknowledged as successful cache publication.
Both actual post_script start and terminal reject self-consistent receipt files whose GPU false disagrees with the actual process GPU integer zero.

launch_eval, run_post_scripts and native_evaluation.begin were not independently saved before adding endpoint guards. Therefore restoring only the three captured functions is not claimed to reproduce all five original failures against the hardened endpoints.
No derived endpoint snapshot or reconstructed full replay is represented as original evidence here. The formal red evidence is the actual first frozen five-case run and recorded source hashes.
No D1-release red claim: the old D1 release did not provide the native CompletionEvent token used by this slice.

The later post/cache/action snapshots are distinct, actually captured full functions from the reviewed D2 draft. Their focused replay results do not reconstruct or replace the original five-case endpoint snapshot limitation.

source_hash_capture.semantics: Shared worktree hashes captured after the 97-case run; not a release/final full-suite source freeze. Other subagents own adjacent portions of existing files.

safety_and_limits: No real GPU, provider, network notification or child process was used; external process/GPU boundaries were synthetic, while Lake, admission, completion, retry, qualification and receipt paths were real.
The completion value is an immutable slots-based two-item sequence compatible with tuple unpacking/equality/indexing, not an actual tuple subclass. Python >=3.9 remains supported.
Source validation does not provide durable per-consumer ACKs or exactly-once notifications across repeated batches/restarts.
Native post-script idempotence is scoped to source AttemptRef plus command text. It is not a scientific observation identity or an artifact/body/environment generation contract.
Native post-script unknown launch/closure leaves nonterminal operational HOLD and has no automatic age-based recovery.
Normal process exit does not prove descendant cleanup; uncooperative external worker writes and attempt-isolated output generations remain outside this slice.
The short transactions use source dependency watches; they do not hold locks across GPU acquisition, Popen, process waits, provider work or checkpoint hashing.
The 97 and 66 targeted runs are not final full-Core/Pro release suites. Main-agent review and overall final validation remain separate.

Source-owned cache guard serializes cooperating retry/reset writers, not malicious SQL/file mutation or a globally atomic artifact/DB snapshot. refresh_metric_snapshot returns None best-effort, so no mirror-publication-success claim is made.
review_boundary_notes: Current qualified success requires global COMPLETE. Existing public state transitions only allow COMPLETE to ARCHIVED, while explicit evaluation retry requires FAILED. A successful A to retry B at notification writes was therefore not demonstrated through legal current APIs, and no invalid FSM mutation was used to invent a behavioral red.

Notification source-owned cache locking is new defensive boundary acceptance. Mutable metric mirrors and config dedup hashes remain caches, not observations or durable acknowledgements. External notification and potentially slow config recovery remain outside the guard.

The actual post-script skip-audit defect is reachable from a failed native A followed by the real evaluation-retry API and B launch. Native skip branches retain logs but no longer perform unowned persistent audit writes.

First unfreezed skip fixture probe yielded one real output-exists failure and one re-entrant test wrapper error: eligibility recursively called itself through real retry validation. The fixture was corrected to a single injection before the final test hash and formal two-behavior-red run; that setup failure is not a product red.

Post-script compute-context tests were authored after the narrow kwargs fix, then run against the actual captured prior action function. That replay exposed two caller-boundary D2-draft failures, not old-release red or API-absence red.
